  "text": "By Saturday morning, Imani had checked the bakery clock six times. Her grandfather pretended not to notice. He dusted the counter with flour, arranged the sesame rings in neat rows, and left one empty chair beside the window.

Nabil arrived just after ten, carrying a cane he insisted he did not need. His eyes went straight to Sami’s drawing beside the till.

“There’s our fence,” he said. “Though Sami made me taller than I ever was.”

Imani brought him the marble. Nabil rolled it between his fingers, holding it up when the yellow streak caught the light.

“Your grandfather and I played with these behind the school,” he told her. “One afternoon, he lost his best marble in the weeds. He looked for it until his mother called him home.”

“And you gave him yours?” Imani asked.

“The next day. I said I had plenty.” Nabil smiled at her grandfather. “I didn’t.”

Her grandfather set a sesame ring on the table between them. “You could have told me.”

“You wouldn’t have taken it.”

For a while they ate and talked about people Imani had never met. She listened, asking questions whenever they forgot to explain a name. At last Nabil placed the marble in her palm.

“It spent enough years in a drawer,” he said. “Take it somewhere it can be seen.”

Imani found a small glass jar on a shelf and set it beside Sami’s drawing. In the afternoon sun, the yellow streak cast a bright mark across the paper fence."
